CorpusProgress.description:
Live progress of one ingest, derived from what is already on B2.

A bulk ingest is one long blocking ``img2dataset.download()`` call, so the
only honest source of "how far along am I" is the output prefix itself:
img2dataset writes each shard's ``_stats.json`` as that shard finishes and
deletes the matching ``_tmp`` input shard, so completed + pending is the
real denominator. Nothing here is timer-driven — a stalled run stops
advancing instead of animating on.
CorpusProgress.title: CorpusProgress

CorpusUpdate.description:
PATCH /corpora/{id} body — only name/description are mutable.

Ingest params are create-time immutable (they determine the shard layout on
B2), so they are intentionally absent here and shown read-only in the UI.
CorpusUpdate.title: CorpusUpdate

the URL, so B2 rejects a body of any other size or type.

Rich metadata (checksums, image/PDF fields) recomputed on demand.

Unlike /metadata (a cheap head_object), this downloads the object to
re-run extraction, so it is billed at the tighter 'write' rate-limit tier
(see runtime/ratelimit.py) to bound egress/cost amplification.

post.description:
Validate a declared upload and hand back a presigned PUT.

The browser uploads the bytes straight to B2 with the returned URL, so they
never traverse this Function — that is what lifts Vercel's ~4.5 MB payload
ceiling. Size and content-type are signed into the URL (see the service).
Confirm an object just uploaded directly to B2 is valid and visible.
